# craftos-mcp

craftos-mcp is a headless CC:Tweaked (ComputerCraft) emulator with an MCP server: the `craftos_*` tools run Lua
programs on emulated computers, read the terminal and every monitor as text, tap buttons, change the world around the
computer and run tests. Run and test every ComputerCraft program in it before saying it works, and before it goes on
a computer in a real game.

## Working with the tools

| Tool                                                                    | Use                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `craftos_info`, `craftos_help`                                          | Call first: what is set up, the versions and addons; the world schema |
| `craftos_write_file`, `craftos_read_file`, `craftos_list_files`         | Workspace files (copied to the root of each computer)                 |
| `craftos_run`                                                           | Run a program in a fresh computer: terminal and monitor text, PNGs    |
| `craftos_test`                                                          | Run `*.test.lua` files with the `ccunit` harness                      |
| `craftos_session_create`, `craftos_ui`, `craftos_act`, `craftos_script` | Drive a running program: read screens as data, tap, type, assert      |
| `craftos_network_create`, `craftos_sim_command`, `craftos_sim_state`    | Several computers over rednet; change and read the world around them  |
| `craftos_seed`, `craftos_advance`, `craftos_trace`, `craftos_clock`     | Pin `math.random`, jump the clock, see what the program saw           |

1. Write the program with `craftos_write_file` and run it with `craftos_run`
   (`monitors: [{name:"top", blocksWide:3, blocksHigh:2}]` attaches a monitor wall; a `world` adds chests, players
   and modded blocks).
2. For a UI, open a session and use `craftos_ui` and `craftos_act` (they read buttons and text as data and wait
   until the program has reacted) rather than screenshots; `craftos_script` runs a whole scenario in one call.
3. Put tests in `*.test.lua` files and run them with `craftos_test`. Each file gets a fresh computer and the global
   `ccunit` (`test`, `eq`, `contains`, `run(program, {script = fn})`, `screen(monitor)`, `touch(monitor, x, y)`).
4. Pick the Minecraft version the user's server runs: 1.18.2 is Lua 5.1 (no `goto`), 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 are Lua 5.2.

The full guide, with the traps that bite real programs, is the `cc-tweaked-dev` skill in `.agents/skills/cc-tweaked-dev/SKILL.md`.

## Setting up the MCP server

The server is `npx -y craftos-mcp serve`, over stdio, and needs Node.js 22 or newer. Its first start downloads the
engine and builds the CC:Tweaked ROM, once (about a minute); the server answers straight away and the tools that run
computers wait for it. The computers' files are the folder the server starts in (`CRAFTOS_WORKSPACE` sets another).
`CRAFTOS_VERSION` (`1.21.1`, `1.20.1` or `1.18.2`) and `CRAFTOS_ADDONS` go in the server's `env`, or in a
`craftos.json` at the project root. On Windows, if a client cannot start `npx`, give it `cmd` with the arguments
`/c npx -y craftos-mcp serve`.

Codex, in `~/.codex/config.toml` (or `.codex/config.toml` in a trusted project), or
`codex mcp add craftos -- npx -y craftos-mcp serve`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.craftos]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"]
# a test run can take longer than the default 60 seconds per call
tool_timeout_sec = 300
```

VS Code with Copilot: the extension (below) registers the server by itself. Without it, `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "craftos": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

Copilot's own config files (`.mcp.json` at the workspace root, `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`) take the same entry
under `mcpServers` instead of `servers`.

Cursor, in `.cursor/mcp.json` (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project); the same `mcpServers` entry goes in
Windsurf's `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` and Claude Desktop's `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "craftos": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"] }
  }
}
```

Gemini CLI, in `.gemini/settings.json` (or `~/.gemini/settings.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "craftos": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"] }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add craftos -- npx -y craftos-mcp serve` (on native Windows,
`claude mcp add craftos -- cmd /c npx -y craftos-mcp serve`), or the plugin, which brings this guide as the
`cc-tweaked-dev` skill: `/plugin marketplace add Akkiruk/craftos-mcp`, then `/plugin install craftos-mcp@craftos-mcp`.

`CRAFTOS_TOOLS=core` offers a lean set of 17 tools instead of all 32, for clients that pay for every tool in every
request.

## Addons (other mods)

Every mod besides CC:Tweaked is an addon. Switch on only the ones the user's modpack has, so a program cannot come to
rely on a peripheral their server lacks: `world.addons` in a world file, `CRAFTOS_ADDONS` in the MCP server's
environment, `"addons"` in craftos.json, or `--addons` on the command line. Each takes addon ids (a list in JSON,
separated by commas elsewhere), `"all"` or `"none"`; with no setting at all, everything the Minecraft version has is
on. A peripheral of an addon that is off fails the world at boot and names the addon. `craftos_info` lists what is on
and `craftos_help` lists every id. An addon only runs on the Minecraft versions its mod came out for; a mod that also
came out for 1.18.2 behaves as its 1.18.2 version on 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 too, so `world.version: "1.18.2"` gives the
most complete simulation.

- Advanced Peripherals 0.7.31r (`advanced-peripherals`): player, energy and environment detectors, chat box, redstone
  integrator, NBT storage, AR controller, ME and RS bridges, from fixtures (`docs/advanced-peripherals.md`,
  `worlds/advanced-peripherals-demo.json`).
- Mekanism 10.2.5 (`mekanism`, `mekanism-generators`): QIO, the Quantum Entangloporter, machines and reactors
  (`docs/mekanism-qio.md`, `worlds/mekanism-qio-demo.json`).
- Create, Tom's Peripherals (GPU screens appear in screenshots), Bigger and Extreme Reactors each have a doc in
  `docs/` and a demo in `worlds/`. CC's own `energy_storage` and `fluid_storage` work on any block
  (`docs/generic-storage.md`).

vhcctweaks (github.com/Akkiruk/vhcctweaks, a server mod for Vault Hunters on Minecraft 1.18.2) is an addon that is
OFF by default and not part of "all": switch it on by naming `vhcctweaks` in world.addons / CRAFTOS_ADDONS /
craftos.json addons, or with `world.vhcctweaks: "2.2.36"` or `"2.2.37"` (`"2.2.35"` also accepted; `false` forces it
off). It needs `world.version: "1.18.2"`. It adds the `ccvault` API (player token balances, transfers with an approval
prompt, the computer's host), the `vhcc` sandboxed file store, lockdown, linked ender modems and the inventory
batch/watch methods; 2.2.37 adds player Gear Power/Temper/reputation/skills/stats reads, items inside container items
and `identify`. The 2.2.37 API is modelled from the mod's spec: identify's roll is the emulator's, not Vault Hunters'
(docs/vhcctweaks.md lists what is simulated and how faithfully).
Linked computers (ender modem links, remote peripherals) run in real time: on a slow or busy machine (many emulated
computers at once) a linked-peripheral call can time out, stall or behave inconsistently, so don't read a flaky
linked test as a bug in the program until it fails on a quiet machine too.

## The VS Code extension

The craftos-mcp extension (`Rogiedoji.craftos-mcp` on the Visual Studio Marketplace, also on Open VSX as
`Rogiedoji/craftos-mcp`) gives Copilot's agent mode the MCP server with no config, adds Run in CraftOS and Debug in
CraftOS (F5) for any `.lua` file, lists `*.test.lua` files in the Testing view, opens `*.world.json` files in a world
editor, and in Cursor and Windsurf offers to write their MCP config. Its command **Add Agent Instructions to
Workspace** writes these instructions for Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Claude Code into the open folder.

## Working on craftos-mcp itself

This section is for changes to the craftos-mcp repository (github.com/Akkiruk/craftos-mcp), not for Lua projects that
use it.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build                               # TypeScript: tsc -b
node scripts/build-rom.mjs --download       # rom/cc-1.121.0 from the real CC:Tweaked jar
node scripts/build-rom.mjs --download 1.18.2  # rom/cc-1.101.3, for Minecraft 1.18.2
npx vitest run                              # the tests; they need the engine and a ROM
npx prettier --check .                      # formatting, as CI checks it
```

`npm run setup` does all of it in one go and also downloads the prebuilt engine for your OS from the latest release
(or build it: `engine/build.cmd` on Windows, `engine/build.sh` elsewhere). CI only builds and checks formatting, so
run the tests locally before a pull request; CONTRIBUTING.md says what a change that executes Lua must come with.

- Engine fork: `engine/` (CMake). Client and protocol: `packages/rawterm`. Orchestration: `packages/runner`. MCP
  tools: `apps/mcp-server`. Command line: `apps/cli`. VS Code extension: `apps/vscode` (its own package and lockfile:
  `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit` inside it).
- The simulation (peripherals, modems, turtles, addons): `rom-overlay/rom/ccsim`. After changing it, copy it into
  each ROM (`cp -r rom-overlay/. rom/cc-1.121.0/`, and `rom/cc-1.101.3/` for 1.18.2) or rebuild the ROMs.
- AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/craftos-mcp.mdc` and the `cc-tweaked-dev`
  skills are generated from `scripts/agent-docs/`: edit those, then run `node scripts/build-agent-docs.mjs`
  (`--check` says whether any file is stale).
